description:
Kent State University’s Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) program provides a comprehensive professional education in athletic training. Our program is designed to develop athletic trainers that are reflective, skilled, and professional practitioners. The program features a rigorous curriculum, hands-on immersive clinical experiences, and an applied research project, providing you with the skills and knowledge to excel in diverse healthcare settings. This program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE) and prepares graduates to be eligible for the Board of Certification (BOC) exam.

The Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) program at Kent State University provides students with a dynamic, immersive learning environment. Here’s what sets our program apart:
*   Comprehensive Curriculum: Our curriculum integrates foundational sciences, clinical skills, and evidence-based practices to ensure you gain a holistic understanding of athletic training.
*   Immersive Clinical Experiences: Gain hands-on experience in diverse clinical settings, including intercollegiate athletics, high schools, outpatient clinics, and physician offices. You’ll work alongside experienced clinicians and apply classroom knowledge to real-world scenarios.
*   Expert Faculty: Learn from dedicated faculty members who are experts in their fields, committed to your academic and professional growth.
*   Research Opportunities: Engage in applied research projects, contributing to the advancement of athletic training knowledge and developing critical inquiry skills.
*   Professional Development: Our program emphasizes professional ethics, interprofessional collaboration, and leadership development, preparing you for a successful career in healthcare.

Upon completion of the Master of Science in Athletic Training program, graduates will be able to:
*   Demonstrate competence in foundational and advanced athletic training knowledge and skills.
*   Apply evidence-based practice principles to clinical decision-making.
*   Exhibit professional behaviors and ethical conduct in all aspects of practice.
*   Collaborate effectively with healthcare professionals and patients.
*   Critically evaluate research and integrate findings into clinical practice.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE)
Program name: Master of Science in Athletic Training

description: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program is a four-year post-baccalaureate professional degree. The curriculum is delivered over 10 semesters (fall, spring, summer) and includes extensive clinical experiences. Graduates of the Au.D. program will possess the knowledge and skills necessary to serve the hearing and balance needs of the public across the lifespan and to obtain professional licensure and certification.
Accreditation status: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at Kent State University is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
Program name: Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.)

description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) in Audiology program provides education and training necessary for future audiologists to enter the profession. Students gain knowledge in areas such as anatomy and physiology of the auditory and vestibular systems, psychoacoustics, diagnostic audiology, amplification and aural rehabilitation, implantable devices, professional issues, research methods, and statistics. Through clinical experiences in the Kent State University Speech and Hearing Clinic and other regional sites, students develop clinical skills in various areas of audiology practice, including diagnostic and rehabilitative audiology across the lifespan. Graduates of the program will be prepared to work in a variety of clinical settings, including hospitals, private practices, schools, and university clinics. The program also prepares students for further doctoral study, specifically the Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) degree. The M.A. in Audiology program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in audiological theory and practice, preparing them for successful careers as audiologists and for continued professional growth and development.
Accreditation status: The Master of Arts (M.A.) education program in audiology at Kent State University is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard, #310, Rockville, MD 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
Program name: Master of Arts in Audiology

description: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at the University of Kansas Medical Center is designed to educate professionals to diagnose, treat and manage individuals with hearing and balance disorders. The curriculum integrates basic science with clinical knowledge and experience to provide the education necessary for a clinical career in audiology. Graduates of the KU Au.D. program are eligible for national certification and state licensure in audiology. They are prepared to work in a variety of settings including hospitals, private practices, schools, universities, industry, and government agencies.
Accreditation status: The Clinical Doctorate (Au.D.) education program in audiology at the University of Kansas Medical Center is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, MD 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Audiology

description: The Autism Spectrum Disorders post-baccalaureate certificate program provides individuals with an in-depth understanding of autism spectrum disorders (ASD) across the lifespan. The certificate focuses on diagnostic characteristics, assessment, evidenced-based intervention strategies and challenges faced by individuals with ASD and their families.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Autism Spectrum Disorders

description: The Master of Science in Accounting (M.S.A.) degree prepares students for accounting careers in public accounting, industry, government and non-profit organizations. The program provides the advanced knowledge necessary for students to develop competencies in professional accounting and fulfill the educational requirements to sit for the CPA exam in Ohio and many other states. The curriculum balances applied accounting topics with professional skills development (e.g., communication, critical thinking, problem solving) to meet the evolving demands of the accounting profession.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting (M.S.A.)

description: The Accounting Analytics Graduate Certificate offers students an understanding of accounting analytics, forensic accounting and data analysis, with a focus on real-world application, while simultaneously developing valuable career skills such as critical thinking, professional skepticism, written and oral communication, teamwork and decision-making. Students develop the ability to apply techniques used to evaluate and analyze data to improve business decision-making, detect fraud and communicate findings. Students also gain hands-on experience using different types of software and tools to analyze accounting data and apply data visualization techniques. The certificate is especially valuable for accounting professionals seeking to update their analytics skills, for professionals seeking to transition to an accounting analytics role and for international students who desire to enhance their understanding of data analytics. The certificate is offered primarily online.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Accounting Analytics
Graduate Certificate in Accounting Fundamentals

description: The Master of Science in Accounting, Business Technology and Analytics (MS-ABTA) degree program provides students with the advanced accounting and analytical skills necessary for careers in accounting, including public accounting, industry, government and not-for-profit organizations. The program trains students to utilize data analytics and business technologies in accounting decision-making. Through this program, students develop expertise in accounting, business analysis, business intelligence, data management and data analytics. This program fulfills the 150-semester hour education requirement for CPA licensure in Ohio and many other states.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting, Business Technology and Analytics

description: The three-year Master of Fine Arts in Acting program at Kent State University is a rigorous, demanding program designed to prepare talented and dedicated individuals for professional careers in theatre, film, and television. A small cohort of highly selective graduate students work with our internationally recognized faculty in a vibrant and supportive atmosphere that fosters both artistic and personal growth. Our approach to training is rooted in Stanislavski-based techniques, but also includes a diverse palette of contemporary and classical acting methods and pedagogies. We are proud to be members of the University/Resident Theatre Association (U/RTA) and The National Alliance of Acting Teachers. Through an intensive array of classes, productions, and workshops, students will hone their skills in voice, speech, movement, stage combat, acting for the camera, Shakespeare, and other relevant areas. The program culminates in a New York City showcase, providing students with direct exposure to industry professionals. Our alumni have gone on to perform on Broadway, off-Broadway, in regional theatres, and in film and television roles. Many have also become successful educators and theatre practitioners.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Acting

description: The Graduate Certificate in Addictions Counseling is for post-master’s or currently enrolled master’s degree students looking to increase their knowledge and skills in the addiction field. The certificate is offered primarily online, with limited on-campus course offerings. The certificate will also help individuals seeking to obtain Ohio Chemical Dependency Counselor Professional Board (OCDPB) licensure as a Licensed Chemical Dependency Counselor III (LCDCIII). The Addictions Counseling program provides students with practical and current information on how to work in addiction treatment settings. Our faculty are active professionals in the field, which means you'll be learning from experts with real-world experience. Many of our courses are offered online, providing you with flexibility in your academic journey.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Addictions Counseling

description: The Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) Post-Master's Certificate prepares graduates of master's degree nursing programs to provide advanced nursing care to individuals (adolescence through geriatrics) with complex acute and/or chronic health conditions. Graduates are eligible to take the national certification examination for AGACNP. Upon completion of certification, graduates are eligible for licensure as an AGACNP in their respective states.
Accreditation status: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master's degree program in nursing, Doctor of Nursing Practice program and post-graduate APRN certificate program at Kent State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education, 655 K Street NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner

description: Adult Gerontology Clinical Nurse Specialists (AGCNS) are advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) who specialize in providing comprehensive care to adult and older adult populations. Their role encompasses direct patient care, disease management, health promotion, and the implementation of evidence-based practices. AGCNS professionals typically work in hospitals, clinics, and long-term care facilities, collaborating with other healthcare providers to optimize patient outcomes. They also serve as mentors and educators, advancing nursing practice through research and leadership.
Accreditation status: Kent State University College of Nursing is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult Gerontology Clinical Nurse Specialist

description:
The Post-Master’s Certificate in Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner is designed for nurses who have already completed a master’s degree in nursing and who desire to become certified as an adult-gerontology primary care nurse practitioner. The program will provide the knowledge and skills necessary for the advanced practice role of the adult-gerontology primary care nurse practitioner and will prepare students to sit for the national certification examination for this role.
The Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner is an advanced practice nurse who provides primary care to adolescents (13 years of age and older) through the entire adult life span, including the elderly. They promote health and provide care for common acute and chronic illnesses within a primary care setting. The curriculum provides a strong theoretical and clinical base in advanced health assessment, pathophysiology, pharmacology, differential diagnosis and disease management.
Upon completion of the Post-Master’s Certificate in Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, graduates are eligible to take the national certification examination provided by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) or the American Academy of Nurse Practitioners (AANP).
Accreditation status: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master’s degree program in nursing, Doctor of Nursing Practice program and post-graduate APRN certificate program at Kent State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education, 655 K Street, NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner

description: The Graduate Certificate in Adult/Adolescent Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) program is a post-master's certificate for master's prepared registered nurses or those enrolled in a master's program. The program is offered in a hybrid format, including didactic coursework, hands-on clinical simulation experiences, and clinical practicum hours. SANE nurses provide compassionate, expert care to patients who have experienced sexual assault. With the number of sexual assault victims on the rise, the need for qualified SANE nurses has never been greater. Kent State University is the only program in Northeast Ohio that offers graduate-level SANE education. The SANE program combines didactic coursework, clinical simulation experiences, and clinical practicum hours in a hybrid format. Students will learn the critical skills needed to provide trauma-informed care for patients who have experienced sexual assault and other forms of interpersonal violence. Students will also learn how to conduct forensic evidence collection, participate in legal proceedings, and provide crisis intervention and support to victims.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult/Adolescent Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner

description: Are you a seasoned accounting professional looking to enhance your expertise, or a recent graduate aspiring to a fulfilling career in the dynamic field of accounting? The online Graduate Certificate in Advanced Accounting at Kent State University is designed for individuals seeking to deepen their understanding of complex accounting principles, preparing them for leadership roles and specialized opportunities within the industry. This certificate program provides a robust curriculum that covers essential topics such as advanced financial accounting, auditing, taxation, and business law, equipping you with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the complexities of modern financial landscapes. Whether you're aiming to meet the educational requirements for CPA licensure, transition into a new accounting specialization, or simply elevate your professional profile, this program offers the flexibility and academic rigor to help you achieve your career aspirations. With a focus on practical application and critical thinking, our expert faculty guides you through real-world scenarios, ensuring you gain insights directly applicable to today's accounting challenges. Invest in your future and position yourself at the forefront of the accounting profession with Kent State's Graduate Certificate in Advanced Accounting.
Accreditation status: Our College of Business Administration is accredited by AACSB International, signifying the highest standard of achievement for business schools worldwide.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Advanced Accounting

description: The Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering (MSAE) degree program provides advanced knowledge in aerospace engineering sub-disciplines, including aerodynamics, flight mechanics, propulsion and structural analysis, and prepares students for careers in the aerospace industry, government research institutions or for doctoral studies. The program is specifically tailored to meet the needs of those students who are interested in pursuing a career path in the aerospace industry. The program emphasizes both theoretical and applied aspects of the aerospace engineering discipline and provides students with the advanced skills necessary to excel in the field. Students can choose to complete either a thesis or non-thesis option.
Program name: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Aerospace Engineering program prepares students to become highly skilled researchers, educators and leaders in the field of aerospace engineering. The program focuses on advanced theoretical and experimental studies, computational methods and design principles relevant to aerospace systems. Students may pursue advanced research in a variety of areas of aerospace engineering, including but not limited to Computational Fluid Dynamics, Aeroacoustics, Flight Dynamics and Control, Aeroelasticity, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Propulsion, and Turbomachinery. Graduates will be equipped to address complex challenges in academia, government laboratories and the aerospace industry.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Aerospace Engineering

description: The Master of Arts degree in Anthropology provides a high-quality graduate education for students interested in advanced studies in anthropology. Students benefit from an experienced faculty with diverse expertise within the four subfields of anthropology (archaeology, biological anthropology, cultural anthropology and linguistic anthropology). The program offers opportunities for students to pursue a thesis or non-thesis option, develop strong research and analytical skills, participate in field schools and gain hands-on experiences in laboratories, museums and cultural resource management projects. The department emphasizes a strong sense of community, collegiality, and opportunities for collaborative research with faculty. Graduates of the program are well prepared for doctoral programs in anthropology or for careers in cultural resource management, museums, forensic anthropology, public health or international development.
Program name: Master of Arts in Anthropology

description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree in Applied Geology provides students with advanced knowledge and research skills in various aspects of applied geology. The program emphasizes quantitative and field-based approaches to problem-solving in areas such as hydrogeology, environmental geology, engineering geology, economic geology and paleontology. Students will engage in independent research culminating in a dissertation that makes an original contribution to the field. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, government agencies, environmental consulting firms, and private industry.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Geology

description: The Master of Arts in Applied Mathematics is designed for students who desire a career in business, government or industry or who wish to pursue doctoral study in applied mathematics. The program focuses on mathematical modeling, computational methods and simulation, and the application of mathematics to solve practical problems across various disciplines.
Program name: Master of Arts in Applied Mathematics

description: The Applied Mathematics master's degree program is a unique interdisciplinary program offered jointly by the Department of Mathematical Sciences, the Department of Computer Science, and the Department of Physics. It combines elements of pure and applied mathematics, numerical analysis, mathematical modeling, scientific computing, and statistical methods. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in applied mathematics and to prepare them for careers in industry, government, or academia. Graduates of this program will be able to: Apply advanced mathematical concepts and techniques to solve real-world problems. Develop and implement mathematical models to analyze complex systems. Use computational tools and software to perform numerical simulations and data analysis. Communicate mathematical ideas and results effectively, both orally and in writing. Pursue further graduate studies or professional careers in applied mathematics or related fields.
Program name: Master of Science in Applied Mathematics

description: The Master of Architecture (M.Arch.) degree is an accredited first-professional degree program in architecture intended for students who have completed an undergraduate degree in any field. The program is committed to developing future professionals who will critically engage with the discipline of architecture and its ethical responsibilities within an increasingly complex world. Students engage in design studios, lecture courses and seminars, which provide knowledge and skills in architectural design, history, theory, technology, professional practice and urbanism.
Accreditation status: The Master of Architecture degree program is accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).
Program name: Master of Architecture

description: The M.S. in Architecture and Environmental Design program is a STEM-designated post-professional degree focused on research related to high-performance buildings and their environmental impact. This program prepares students for careers in research-intensive design, consulting, and industry positions. It also provides a foundation for doctoral studies. Students work with faculty on topics related to building energy performance, daylighting and human behavior, sustainable design, building integrated photovoltaics, digital design and fabrication, high-performance facades, urban climate, and resilience. This program will equip you with the skills and knowledge necessary to address the pressing challenges of climate change and resource depletion, shaping the future of sustainable architecture.
Program name: Master of Science in Architecture and Environmental Design

description: The Master of Arts in Art Education program at Kent State University prepares students for professional careers in teaching art and provides leadership in the field of art education in museums, public and private schools, and community art settings. The program also serves as a strong foundation for doctoral studies. Art educators in the M.A. program explore innovative teaching strategies, contemporary art curriculum development, critical theory in art education, and diverse research methodologies. The program emphasizes artistic inquiry, research, and critical thinking within the context of current issues in art education. Graduates of the program are prepared to assume leadership positions as highly qualified art teachers and advocates for art education. The program offers both on-campus and fully online options.
Program name: Master of Arts in Art Education

description: The Master of Arts in Art History provides students with a broad and rigorous foundation in the history of art. Students delve into various periods, cultures and theoretical approaches, developing critical thinking, research and analytical skills essential for advanced study and professional careers. The program offers both thesis and non-thesis options, allowing students to tailor their academic path to their individual goals. Graduates are prepared for doctoral studies, careers in museums, galleries, academia or other art-related fields.
Program name: Master of Arts in Art History

description: The Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence program provides students with the fundamental concepts and principles of Artificial Intelligence and advanced topics in a variety of related areas including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, knowledge representation, data science, etc. The program provides the necessary background and skills in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to prepare students for successful careers in industry, research, or academia. Graduates of the program will be qualified to hold positions such as AI Software Developer, AI Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, etc., in various organizations from government to private industry. Students will gain experience with Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow and other related tools.
Program name: Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence

description: The Master of Science in Aviation Management and Logistics program provides the advanced scientific training and management skills needed to lead aviation-based organizations. Graduates of the program are prepared for a wide range of leadership and management careers in the aviation industry, including airport management, airline operations, air traffic control management, aerospace logistics, and aviation consulting. This program can be pursued on a full-time or part-time basis on the Kent Campus. The Aviation Management and Logistics curriculum requires a minimum of 32 credit hours.
Program name: Master of Science in Aviation Management and Logistics

description: The Behavioral Intervention Specialist graduate certificate helps prepare students for careers where they serve individuals with challenging behavior, including individuals with developmental disabilities such as autism spectrum disorders, intellectual disabilities, and related conditions. Students learn to use evidence-based behavioral assessment and intervention strategies. Graduates are prepared for positions as behavioral intervention specialists in school, agency, clinical and home settings. The certificate also serves students who want to continue on to the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) Master of Arts (M.A.) degree and meet the coursework requirements to apply for certification as a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA®).
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Behavioral Intervention Specialist

description:
The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biological Sciences is an advanced studies degree for students interested in a research-oriented career or in further doctoral studies in the biological sciences. The program prepares graduates for careers in research, teaching and further graduate study.
The Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics concentration allows students to gain a deeper understanding of the genetic and molecular underpinnings of cellular processes through advanced coursework and hands-on laboratory experience. Research opportunities are available in various areas, including molecular biology, cell signaling, gene regulation, immunology, developmental biology and cancer biology.
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences - Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics

description: The Ph.D. in Biological Sciences provides students with broad training in biology and specialized training in a research concentration. Graduates with the Ph.D. in Biological Sciences are prepared for careers in research, teaching and related fields in academia, industry and government. Students may choose from two concentrations: Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics, and Ecology and Evolutionary Biology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biological Sciences - Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics

description: The Master of Science degree in Biological Sciences with a concentration in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at Kent State University provides students with advanced knowledge and research experience in areas such as ecology, evolution, behavior, population genetics, conservation biology, systematics, biogeography and environmental science. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in academia, government agencies, non-profit organizations and private industry, as well as for further graduate studies at the doctoral level.
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences - Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

description: The Ph.D. program with a concentration in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology provides students with rigorous training in ecological and evolutionary theory, statistics, and experimental design within a strong research framework. Students conduct original research under the mentorship of faculty whose interests span a wide range of ecological and evolutionary topics, including conservation biology, community ecology, behavioral ecology, molecular evolution, phylogenetics, population genetics, and evolutionary genomics. The program prepares students for careers in academia, government agencies, and private industry.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biological Sciences - Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

description: The Master of Science in Biological Sciences is an advanced degree designed for students who wish to pursue a career in biology, education or enter a doctoral program. The Integrative Physiology and Neurobiology concentration provides students with opportunities to conduct research in human and animal physiological systems and disease, cellular and molecular physiology, neurobiology and behavior, and sensory biology.
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences - Integrative Physiology and Neurobiology

description: The Master of Arts in Biology program provides graduate students with advanced training in biology. The M.A. program is a non-thesis master's degree program that prepares students for employment in a variety of scientific and related fields, or for further graduate studies. The curriculum is flexible and can be customized to fit the interests and career goals of each student. Students gain a deeper understanding of biological principles, develop critical thinking and research skills, and learn to effectively communicate scientific information. Graduates are well-prepared for roles in research, education, biotechnology, environmental science, and other science-related professions.
Program name: Master of Arts in Biology

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in medical and allied health fields, biotechnology, pharmaceutical sciences, and biomedical research. The program emphasizes basic biomedical research and professional development, focusing on the development of critical thinking, problem-solving and communication skills relevant to scientific inquiry. Students may choose from three concentrations: Cellular and Molecular Biology, Human Movement Science and Neuroscience. Students interested in pursuing a doctoral degree (Ph.D.) may transition to the Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. program after completing the M.S. degree. A 4+1 combined B.S./M.S. degree is also available.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Cellular and Molecular Biology

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Biomedical Sciences focuses on research-intensive training in the biomedical sciences, spanning from the molecular and cellular levels to whole organisms. The curriculum builds a strong foundation in a broad range of biomedical areas. Students select a concentration in Cellular and Molecular Biology, Environmental Pathobiology or Neuroscience, which allows for advanced specialized training aligned with their research interests and career goals. Students choose a faculty advisor who guides their dissertation research project. The program prepares students for careers in academia, industry, research and development, and government agencies.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Cellular and Molecular Biology

description: The Human Evolutionary Biology (HEB) concentration focuses on the study of human and primate evolution from a comparative perspective, investigating the biological and behavioral processes that characterize humans and their primate relatives. Faculty research interests include hominin paleontology, evolutionary morphology, primate behavioral ecology, human behavioral ecology, primate conservation and evolutionary medicine. Students are trained to conduct interdisciplinary research within the department and in collaboration with colleagues across campus. Research opportunities include fieldwork at fossil sites in Kenya and Tanzania, analyses of existing fossil and primate skeletal collections and behavioral studies of captive primates. Research in the HEB concentration leverages close ties with the Kent State University Museum and with the Cleveland Museum of Natural History.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Human Evolutionary Biology

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences is offered to students with diverse backgrounds in biological and physical sciences who are interested in pursuing research careers in biomedical sciences or allied health professions. This program provides students with fundamental knowledge in biomedical sciences while offering advanced courses and research training in specialized areas. Graduates are prepared for doctoral studies in biomedical sciences, medical school or other health professional programs and positions in academic or industrial research.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Neurosciences

description: The Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences with a concentration in Neurosciences program focuses on fundamental and translational research in brain function and dysfunction, with an emphasis on molecular, cellular, anatomical, physiological and behavioral mechanisms. The program prepares students for careers in academic research, government or industry. Students in this program are trained in multiple areas of neuroscience, including molecular, cellular, systems and behavioral neuroscience, and are expected to develop an individualized research program, write grant proposals, publish scientific articles and present at national meetings.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Neurosciences

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences focuses on research-intensive training and career preparation in biomedical research. The Biomedical Sciences program offers concentrations in Cell and Molecular Biology, Neuroscience, Pharmacology and Physiology. The Pharmacology concentration prepares students for careers in research or academia at universities, pharmaceutical companies or government agencies. The concentration provides students with foundational training in pharmacology, including pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics and toxicology, as well-as hands-on research experience.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Pharmacology

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Biomedical Sciences is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in biomedical research or further study in doctoral programs in biomedical sciences and health professional schools. The M.S. degree requires students to acquire knowledge in biomedical sciences through graduate-level coursework and develop skills in scientific research through the completion of a thesis. The program offers three interdisciplinary concentrations: Cellular and Molecular Biology, Neuroscience and Physiology. The program is offered on the Kent campus and at the Northeast Ohio Medical University (NEOMED). The Physiology Interdisciplinary concentration focuses on the study of the function of living systems and their components, ranging from the molecular and cellular level to integrated systems physiology, which is applicable to many health-related professions and research areas. The program provides a broad curriculum covering topics such as cardiovascular, renal, neuro- and respiratory physiology, endocrinology, metabolism and immunology. The program includes coursework, seminars and mentored research experiences that provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue doctoral studies, enter health professional schools or work in biomedical research.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Physiology Interdisciplinary

description: The Master of Science in Chemistry degree program prepares students for careers in chemical industries and related fields or for further graduate study toward a Ph.D. in Chemistry. The program emphasizes both advanced coursework and original research. Thesis and non-thesis options are available.
Program name: Master of Science in Chemistry
Master of Arts in Chemistry

Concentration name: Applied Artificial Intelligence, Bioinformatics, Data Science, Software Engineering
description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Computer Science is a research-oriented program offering advanced study in computer science. The program curriculum includes advanced coursework, seminars, comprehensive examinations and original research. Thesis and non-thesis options are available. The thesis option focuses on advanced research and culminates in the preparation and defense of a master's thesis. The non-thesis option focuses on advanced coursework and requires a comprehensive examination. Students completing the M.S. degree are prepared for positions in industry, research and development, or for further graduate study in a doctoral program.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science

description: The Master of Arts in Computer Science degree is offered through the Department of Computer Science. The program prepares students to meet the demand for advanced knowledge in computer science. Students develop skills in areas such as algorithms, artificial intelligence, computer architecture, computer graphics, computer networks, database systems, distributed computing, operating systems, programming languages, software engineering and theoretical computer science. Graduate students are trained for positions in business, industry, education and government. The M.A. in Computer Science program is excellent preparation for doctoral study.
Program name: Master of Arts in Computer Science

description: The Master of Arts degree in Criminology and Criminal Justice is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge of theory, research methods and statistics that will prepare them for future study in doctoral programs, as well as for careers in criminal justice, government, research and policy analysis. The program curriculum includes coursework in criminological theory, research methods, advanced statistics, and electives in areas such as policing, corrections, victimization, juvenile delinquency, race and crime, and drugs and crime.
Program name: Master of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice

description:
The Master of Arts in English degree program at Kent State University provides students with advanced study in the fields of literary and cultural criticism, rhetorical and composition studies, creative writing and pedagogy. The program is designed for students who wish to pursue further graduate study leading to the Ph.D. degree or who wish to teach at the secondary or college level.

Graduates of this program will be able to:
*   Demonstrate knowledge of various literary periods, genres, and critical theories.
*   Analyze and interpret complex texts from diverse cultural and historical contexts.
*   Conduct independent research and produce scholarly work in the field of English.
*   Communicate effectively in written and oral forms, demonstrating advanced rhetorical skills.
*   Apply pedagogical theories and practices in teaching English language and literature (for students in the Concentration for Teachers).
Program name: Master of Arts in English (Concentration for Teachers)

description: The M.A. in English, Literature and Writing combines focused study in literary history, theory, and criticism with intensive coursework in rhetoric, composition, and creative writing. It provides students with a broad and deep foundation in English studies, as well as the opportunity to specialize and hone their skills in particular areas. The Literature and Writing MA program at Kent State University offers a dynamic and rigorous curriculum designed to cultivate advanced literary and rhetorical understanding and sophisticated writing skills. Our program emphasizes: A comprehensive study of literary history, theory, and criticism. Advanced training in various writing forms, including academic, professional, and creative writing. Opportunities for interdisciplinary study and research. Preparation for further graduate study (Ph.D.) or careers in teaching, publishing, editing, technical writing, and other writing-intensive professions. A diverse and supportive academic community with dedicated faculty mentors.
Program name: Master of Arts in English (Literature and Writing)

description: The Master of Arts degree in Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) is designed for students who wish to pursue careers in teaching English to speakers of other languages in the U.S. and abroad, with a particular focus on post-secondary teaching and teacher education. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and pedagogical applications. Students acquire a strong foundation in second language acquisition, linguistics, sociolinguistics, methods of TESL and practical experience through supervised teaching. The program prepares graduates to teach English as a second language, as well as for further graduate studies at the doctoral level.
Program name: Master of Arts in Teaching English as a Second Language
Master of Science in Geography

description: The Master of Arts in History program is designed for students who wish to deepen their knowledge of history and historical methodology. The program offers advanced study in various historical fields, preparing students for doctoral work, careers in education, public history, or other fields requiring strong research, analytical and communication skills. Students develop a sophisticated understanding of historical processes, interpretations and historiography, and hone their abilities to conduct original research, critically evaluate sources and present their findings effectively.
Program name: Master of Arts in History

description: The Master of Liberal Studies (L.S.M.) program at Kent State University is a highly flexible, individualized interdisciplinary graduate program designed for students who want to broaden their knowledge in the arts, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. The L.S.M. is a 30-credit-hour master’s degree program that offers students a wide range of academic choices and opportunities to explore diverse intellectual interests and create a custom-designed curriculum relevant to their personal and professional goals. The program is ideal for students who wish to pursue a graduate degree but whose interests do not fit neatly into one discipline or a traditional master's degree program. It emphasizes critical thinking, intellectual curiosity, and interdisciplinary scholarship, preparing students for diverse career paths or further doctoral study. Students in the L.S.M. program will: Develop advanced critical thinking and analytical skills through exposure to diverse academic disciplines. Cultivate interdisciplinary knowledge and perspectives by integrating insights from the arts, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. Enhance research and communication skills through scholarly inquiry and effective presentation of ideas. Prepare for diverse professional opportunities requiring adaptable problem-solving and broad intellectual engagement. Explore new avenues for personal and intellectual growth, fostering a lifelong commitment to learning.
Program name: Master of Liberal Studies (L.S.M.)

description: The Master of Arts in Mathematics for Secondary Teachers program is designed for secondary school mathematics teachers who desire to broaden their knowledge of mathematics and enhance their teaching skills. Graduates of the program will be better-prepared to teach mathematics courses from Algebra I through calculus, as well as have the background to lead curriculum development within their schools and districts. The program provides the mathematical background needed for a secondary school teacher to earn college credit for teaching dual enrollment courses in high school and fulfills content requirements for licensure renewal.
Program name: Master of Arts in Mathematics for Secondary Teachers

description: The Master of Arts in Mathematics degree program develops students' mathematical knowledge and problem-solving abilities. Students choose a concentration in Applied Mathematics, Pure Mathematics or Statistics. Graduates of the program are prepared for doctoral studies in mathematics or statistics, teaching at the community college level or employment in business or industry.
Program name: Master of Arts in Pure Mathematics

description: The M.S. in Pure Mathematics program is primarily for students wishing to pursue a Ph.D. in Mathematics. The program can also serve as a terminal degree for those seeking a career in academia at a small college or in an industry requiring a strong mathematical background. The program has specific requirements that overlap substantially with the Ph.D. program.
Program name: Master of Science in Pure Mathematics

description: The Master of Arts degree in French prepares students for careers as language professionals in the public and private sectors, for teaching at the high school and junior college level, and for doctoral studies in French. The program emphasizes advanced linguistic and cultural competence through coursework in French and francophone literatures and cultures, second language acquisition and pedagogical methods. The program features two tracks: one in French and Francophone Literatures and Cultures and one in French and Francophone Literatures and Cultures with a K-12 teaching focus, with options for a thesis or non-thesis project. The program offers graduate assistantships to qualified students. For additional information, see the French program website.
Program name: Master of Arts in French

description: The Master of Arts degree in Latin is designed to provide advanced training for students who wish to pursue scholarly research in classical languages, literature and culture, or to enhance their skills for teaching Latin at the secondary level. Students completing the MA in Latin are prepared for doctoral study in classical philology at other institutions; they also gain additional skills and credentials for teaching Latin at the secondary level.
Program name: Master of Arts in Latin

description: The Spanish M.A. program provides students with advanced knowledge of Spanish and Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics or Spanish as a second/foreign language. The program prepares students for Ph.D. studies, careers in higher education and secondary education, as well as careers in government and private sectors. Graduates of this program will be able to demonstrate: Advanced proficiency in the Spanish language in all four skill areas (reading, writing, speaking and listening). Advanced knowledge and critical understanding of Spanish and Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics or Spanish as a second/foreign language. Ability to conduct independent research in the field of Spanish/Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics, or Spanish as a second/foreign language and articulate results both orally and in writing. Ability to apply appropriate theoretical and methodological approaches to a variety of critical issues in Spanish and Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics, or Spanish as a second/foreign language. Ability to formulate and present scholarly arguments about Spanish and Spanish American literature and culture, Iberian and Latin American linguistics, or Spanish as a second/foreign language.
Program name: Master of Arts in Spanish

description: The Master of Arts in Translation program provides professional training to prepare students for careers in translation, localization and related fields. It also prepares students who wish to pursue doctoral studies in translation. The program’s main goals are to educate students in translation theory and practice and to develop students’ high-level translation proficiency and cultural competence. The program offers optional concentrations in Literary Translation, Localizing for Global Audiences, Translation for Global Health and Medicine, Translation for Specific Purposes and Translation Studies. The Master of Arts in Translation is a fully online program. The flexible online format allows students to study from any geographic location with a computer and internet access.
Program name: Master of Arts in Translation

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Physics offers students advanced studies in various areas of theoretical and experimental physics. Students conduct research with faculty and are prepared for doctoral studies or careers in industry. The Department of Physics offers research opportunities in various fields, including astronomy, condensed matter physics, high energy physics, materials science, medical physics, nuclear physics and theoretical physics.
Program name: Master of Science in Physics

description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in Physics is offered to students who wish to broaden their knowledge of physics, either as a terminal degree or as preparation for doctoral studies. The program provides a general background in theoretical and experimental physics, with thesis and non-thesis options. Master's degree holders typically find employment in private industry or government laboratories.
Program name: Master of Arts in Physics

description: The Master of Arts in Political Science program provides students with advanced knowledge of political institutions, processes, and theories. Students develop critical thinking, research, and analytical skills through rigorous coursework, preparing them for careers in government, non-profit organizations, education, and further doctoral studies. The program offers comprehensive training in various subfields of political science, including American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, and public policy. Faculty members are active scholars and dedicated mentors, committed to fostering intellectual growth and professional development.
Program name: Master of Arts in Political Science

description: The Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) degree is an applied professional degree that prepares students for management positions in the public and nonprofit sectors. As a regionally accredited program (NASPAA), the Kent State M.P.A. program provides a broad understanding of the public and nonprofit sectors while developing managerial competencies for effective and ethical leadership. The M.P.A. program emphasizes public policy, public management, analytical methods, financial management and organizational management. Students learn to critically analyze public problems, understand how to implement public policy, manage public programs, develop financial literacy and communicate effectively. All students are required to complete a professional project or thesis.
Accreditation status: Regionally accredited program (NASPAA)
Program name: Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.)

description: A Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in philosophy from Kent State prepares you for further graduate study in philosophy, or for careers where strong analytical skills and clear communication are crucial. Our M.A. program has a strong track record of placing graduates into top Ph.D. programs and teaching positions in philosophy. Students interested in Bioethics and Medical Humanities can pursue the M.A. with a concentration in those areas. The department also participates in the interdisciplinary Medical Humanities Research Group and supports numerous conferences and workshops each year. Our philosophy graduate students have a variety of opportunities to participate in departmental colloquia, conferences, and independent studies with faculty. The department offers a wide range of courses in all the main areas of philosophy, including history of philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, social and political philosophy, philosophy of mind, philosophy of language, and aesthetics.
Program name: Master of Arts in Philosophy

description: The Master of Arts (M.A.) degree in Psychological Science prepares students for doctoral work in various areas of psychology (e.g., clinical, cognitive, developmental, experimental, social), and for careers that require research skills (e.g., survey research, program evaluation). It is a research-intensive program. Students will learn how to design and conduct research, analyze data and write research reports. A thesis is required.
Program name: Master of Arts in Clinical Psychology

description: The Master of Arts degree in Psychological Sciences offers students advanced training in various areas of psychology. This program provides students with the opportunity to pursue their interests in psychology at an advanced level beyond the undergraduate curriculum. Students will be trained in the scientific method, psychological theory and the application of psychological knowledge through courses in methodology, statistics, theory and practice. There are two concentrations: General and User Experience.
Program name: Master of Arts in Psychological Sciences

description: The Master of Arts in Sociology degree program provides students with advanced theoretical training, research methods and data analysis skills. The program prepares students for careers in applied social research, teaching at the community college level or further graduate study in a Ph.D. program. The program offers a thesis and a non-thesis option. The thesis option is designed for students considering further graduate work beyond the master’s degree. The non-thesis option is designed for students seeking careers in applied social research or teaching at the community college level. Both options require a comprehensive examination.
Program name: Master of Arts in Sociology

description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Educational Technology program prepares graduates to become leaders in the field of educational technology across diverse settings, including K-12 schools, higher education, corporate training, and non-profit organizations. Students gain expertise in designing, developing, implementing, and evaluating technology-rich learning environments. The program focuses on instructional design, emerging technologies, multimedia development, data analysis, and leadership in educational technology. Through hands-on projects, research, and practical experiences, students learn to integrate technology effectively to enhance teaching and learning, foster innovation, and address contemporary educational challenges. This program offers four distinct specializations to fit your career goals. Specializations are not concentrations, but rather a group of courses you select that align with your career goals.
Program name: Master of Education in Educational Technology

description: The Master of Science in Exercise Physiology prepares students for careers in clinical, research, industry and academic settings. Through a combination of coursework and hands-on experiences, students gain advanced knowledge and skills in exercise science. The curriculum emphasizes the physiological responses and adaptations to exercise, exercise testing and prescription, and research methods in exercise physiology. Graduates are prepared for positions such as clinical exercise physiologists, exercise specialists, strength and conditioning coaches, wellness directors and researchers. The program also provides a strong foundation for those pursuing doctoral studies in exercise physiology or related fields.
Program name: Master of Science in Exercise Physiology

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Exercise Physiology is designed for students seeking advanced academic and research training beyond the master’s degree. The program emphasizes the scientific basis of exercise physiology and provides students with the theoretical knowledge and practical research experience necessary to become independent scholars and researchers. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, research institutions, and various health-related fields. The program requires completion of coursework, comprehensive examinations, and a dissertation based on original research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Exercise Physiology

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Higher Education Administration prepares students to serve in administrative and leadership positions in a variety of postsecondary institutions. The program helps students develop a comprehensive understanding of theory and research related to college students, faculty, organization, leadership, finance, governance, and policy. Students learn to apply higher education research and scholarship to practice and policy issues in their professional roles. The program prepares students to become researchers through comprehensive coursework in research methods and quantitative and qualitative research. Students also develop expertise in an area of concentration through their coursework and dissertation research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Higher Education Administration

description: The Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs (HESA) Education Specialist (Ed.S.) program prepares knowledgeable, reflective and ethical mid-career professionals to lead colleges, universities and related higher education organizations. The Ed.S. program is for individuals who have already earned a master's degree in higher education or a related field and want to build advanced knowledge and leadership skills for higher education administration practice. This program requires 30 credit hours beyond the master’s degree and can be completed in two to three years of study.
Program name: Education Specialist in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs

description: Kent State University's Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs program prepares professionals for leadership roles in colleges and universities.
Program name: Master of Education in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs

description: Kent State University's Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Interprofessional Leadership prepares leaders across a variety of fields to effectively collaborate, innovate, and drive positive change within complex organizations and systems. This fully online, cohort-based program emphasizes experiential learning, practical application, and a strong commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Through a blend of rigorous coursework, hands-on projects, and a culminating dissertation, students will develop advanced critical thinking, research, and communication skills essential for addressing contemporary challenges in their respective professions. The program is designed for working professionals seeking to advance their careers and make a significant impact in areas such as healthcare, education, non-profit management, public service, and business. Graduates of the Ed.D. in Interprofessional Leadership program will be equipped to: Lead diverse teams and foster collaborative environments; Design and implement innovative solutions to complex organizational challenges; Apply ethical principles and social justice perspectives to leadership practices; Conduct rigorous research to inform decision-making and drive continuous improvement; Advocate for systemic change and contribute to the advancement of their fields.
Program name: Doctor of Education in Interprofessional Leadership

description: The Master of Arts degree in Learning Science is designed for professionals and students interested in developing the skills to advance theory and practice of learning. The program focuses on understanding how humans learn and developing instructional innovations that apply learning science principles. It provides students with advanced knowledge and skills in learning theory, research methods, and design of learning environments. The curriculum emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach, drawing from cognitive psychology, educational psychology, computer science, and instructional design. Graduates are prepared for a variety of roles in education, training, corporate learning and development, and research settings.
Program name: Master of Arts in Learning Science

description: The Learning Science Ph.D. program prepares scholars and researchers for positions in universities, research and policy organizations, and educational or corporate settings. Students in this program will study how people learn in different contexts. They will learn how to design, implement, and evaluate learning environments, experiences, and technologies to improve learning outcomes. Graduates of the program will address complex problems through the application of advanced research methods and theoretical perspectives grounded in the learning sciences. The Learning Science Ph.D. program provides students with the opportunity to: Engage in the systematic study of learning across various contexts. Acquire skills in designing, implementing, and evaluating learning environments. Develop advanced research methodologies and theoretical frameworks. Contribute to the field of learning sciences through scholarly research and publications. Prepare for leadership roles in academia, research, and educational development.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Learning Science

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Nutrition at Kent State University is designed to prepare graduates for careers in research, education, clinical and community nutrition settings, as well as for further graduate study in nutrition or related fields. The program provides advanced knowledge in nutrition science, research methods and professional practice. Students in the program also develop critical thinking, communication and problem-solving skills necessary for professional success.
Program name: Master of Science in Nutrition
Master of Education in Reading Specialization
Master of Education in Research, Measurement, and Statistics

description: The Ph.D. in Research, Measurement, and Statistics (RMS) is designed to prepare students for careers in applied educational and psychological research, measurement, and statistics. RMS graduates acquire knowledge and skills in research design, measurement and assessment, and quantitative analysis. The program is committed to developing scholars with expertise in substantive areas and with competence in the application of methodological tools to solve pressing educational and psychological problems. The RMS program focuses on developing the knowledge and skills necessary for the production and consumption of educational and psychological research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Research, Measurement, and Statistics

description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) degree in School Counseling prepares students to work as school counselors in elementary, middle and high schools. The program combines knowledge and skills from education, counseling and psychology. Graduates are prepared to meet the academic, career, social and emotional needs of all students. Upon completion of the school counseling program, students are eligible to apply for the Ohio school counselor license. The program meets the 2016 Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) standards.
Accreditation status: The program meets the 2016 Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) standards.
Program name: Master of Education in School Counseling

description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in School Psychology program prepares graduates to become licensed school psychologists for employment in educational settings from pre-kindergarten through grade 12. The program is committed to developing culturally competent school psychologists who utilize prevention and intervention services. The program is designed to integrate the scientific and professional practice knowledge bases to provide a comprehensive training experience. Students apply and integrate coursework in the preparation of school psychology best practices in supervised clinical field experiences.
Accreditation status: The School Psychology program is approved by the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP).
Program name: Master of Education in School Psychology

description: The Education Specialist (Ed.S.) degree in School Psychology prepares candidates to work in schools providing comprehensive psychological services to children, families and school personnel. This program is for individuals interested in professional practice as a school psychologist. Students develop competencies in assessment, intervention, consultation, program development and evaluation. Through extensive supervised practice in school settings, students learn to apply psychological principles to educational issues concerning learning, behavior, social-emotional development and mental health. The program requires 78 credit hours of graduate coursework, including an internship. Graduates of the Ed.S. program meet the academic requirements for licensure as a school psychologist in Ohio and are eligible for the Nationally Certified School Psychologist (NCSP) credential through the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP). Students pursuing the Ed.S. degree are not required to complete a master's thesis.
Accreditation status: Approved by the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP).
Program name: Education Specialist in School Psychology

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in School Psychology prepares doctoral students for advanced professional practice as psychologists in school and other settings. The program is committed to a scientist-practitioner model of training that fosters both research and practice competencies. The program provides students with broad and general training in psychology and school psychology, and prepares them for leadership roles in the field. Students typically pursue either the APA-accredited general school psychology training program or a neuropsychology subspecialty track within the school psychology program. The program follows a cohort model and provides students with a sequence of integrated courses and experiences grounded in current theory, research and practice. Faculty are dedicated to providing students with high quality instruction and professional supervision in research, assessment, intervention, consultation and prevention across multiple ecological levels. The program promotes an understanding of diversity issues and culturally sensitive practice in all aspects of its training model. Students complete required coursework, research experience, practica, a dissertation and an internship. Graduates of the program are eligible for licensure as psychologists in Ohio and other states, as well as licensure as school psychologists.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA)
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in School Psychology

description: The Master of Arts in Teaching (M.A.T.) in Secondary Education provides an accelerated program of study for individuals who hold a bachelor's degree in a content area and seek initial licensure to teach at the secondary level. Candidates complete an intensive program that culminates in initial teaching licensure and a master's degree in as few as 18 months of full-time study.
Program name: Master of Arts in Teaching Secondary Education

description: The Master of Education in Special Education (M.Ed.) program is designed for teachers who seek to advance their knowledge and skills in special education. The program offers options for licensed teachers to obtain K-12 Intervention Specialist Licensure or to pursue the Educational Diagnostician Concentration. The program helps develop leaders in the field of special education who will advocate for individuals with exceptionalities.
Accreditation status: Initial teacher licensure programs and advanced education programs for licensed educators are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and approved by the Ohio Department of Higher Education (ODHE).
Program name: Master of Education in Special Education

Concentration name: Gifted Education, Low Incidence Disabilities, Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: The Education Specialist (Ed.S.) degree program in Special Education offers advanced study beyond the master’s degree, but short of the doctoral degree, for education professionals who wish to enhance their skills in areas of special education, curriculum, assessment, research and related areas. The Ed.S. degree is a 30-credit-hour program that includes an exit requirement of an Ed.S. project or thesis. The Ed.S. degree is offered on the Kent campus and online. Students may select a concentration in Gifted Education, Low Incidence Disabilities or Mild/Moderate Disabilities.
Program name: Education Specialist in Special Education

Concentration name: Applied Behavior Analysis, Deaf Education, Early Intervention, Intervention Specialist (Mild/Moderate or Moderate/Intensive Needs), Learning and Technology, Multicultural Special Education, Transition to Adulthood
description: The Ph.D. in Special Education provides advanced study for students who wish to become leaders in the field. The program is designed to prepare highly qualified special educators for positions as university faculty members, researchers and administrators in public schools, private agencies and government. The program features coursework in research methods, statistics, core areas of special education, and an area of specialization.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Special Education

description: The Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Educational Psychology provides students with foundational knowledge in human learning, development, motivation, and research methods and statistics. This program prepares students to apply psychological principles to educational contexts, conduct research, and contribute to evidence-based practice in various settings, including schools, universities, government agencies, and research organizations. Graduates are well-prepared for roles as educational researchers, evaluators, program developers, and data analysts. The program also serves as excellent preparation for doctoral studies in educational psychology or related fields.
Program name: Master of Education in Educational Psychology

description: The Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Interprofessional Leadership is designed for experienced professionals and administrators who are seeking to develop their leadership knowledge and skills to address complex problems, foster collaboration and drive positive change within diverse organizational and community contexts. Students will learn how to lead effectively, foster innovation and promote equity across various sectors, including education, healthcare, non-profit organizations and government agencies. This program is designed to develop practitioner-scholars who can apply advanced research, ethical decision-making and transformative leadership practices to create meaningful impact in their respective fields. Students will develop their ability to critically analyze complex challenges, design and implement evidence-based solutions and collaborate with diverse stakeholders to achieve shared goals.
Program name: Doctor of Education (Ed.D.)

description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (D.N.P.) degree program is a practice-focused doctorate designed to prepare advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) and master's-prepared registered nurses for the highest level of clinical nursing practice. Graduates of the D.N.P. program are prepared to translate evidence into practice, apply evidence-based knowledge and implement programs to improve healthcare outcomes, assume leadership roles in the healthcare system and demonstrate competence in advanced nursing practice.
Accreditation status: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (D.N.P.) program is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE), 655 K Street, NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.
Program name: Doctor of Nursing Practice (D.N.P.)

description: Podiatric Medicine is a branch of the medical sciences devoted to the study of human movement in health and disease and the care of the human foot, ankle, and related structures of the leg. It requires a doctor of podiatric medicine (D.P.M.) degree. As an integral member of the healthcare delivery team, the podiatric physician and surgeon is educated and trained to diagnose and treat conditions affecting the foot, ankle, and structures of the leg. This includes conditions related to bone, joints, ligaments, muscles, tendons, nerves, skin, and nails. Podiatrists provide both medical and surgical treatment options, including the prescription of medication, physical therapy, orthotics, prosthetics, and advanced surgical procedures. Podiatrists care for patients of all ages, from infants to the elderly. Podiatric physicians are trained in four years of graduate-level education at one of eleven colleges of podiatric medicine (CPM's) in the United States. Following the D.P.M. degree, all graduates enter into a post-graduate residency program, which are typically 3 years in length. There are a variety of residency programs including Podiatric Medicine and Surgery (PMSR), with or without Reconstructive Rearfoot and Ankle (RRA) credentials. The completion of a residency is required for board certification and to practice in most states. D.P.M.'s work in hospitals, private practice, academic institutions, and federal government agencies. Their patient populations include athletes, diabetics, and pediatric patients. Many podiatrists specialize in surgery, wound care, sports medicine, or biomechanics. Approximately 8% of podiatrists are women.
Program name: Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (D.P.M.)

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Accounting program at Kent State University is designed to prepare students for successful careers as accounting researchers and educators in academic institutions. The program provides rigorous training in research methodologies, advanced accounting theories, and quantitative analysis, enabling graduates to contribute original knowledge to the field of accounting. Students will work closely with faculty mentors, engage in cutting-edge research, and develop the pedagogical skills necessary for effective teaching. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and the development of an independent research agenda.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Accounting

description: The Ph.D. in Finance program at Kent State University is designed to prepare highly qualified individuals for academic careers in finance at major universities and other institutions, both domestically and internationally. Our graduates gain tenure-track faculty positions at institutions such as the University of Colorado, University of Kentucky, and DePaul University, among others. The program emphasizes the development of research skills through doctoral seminars and independent study with faculty, and requires students to apply quantitative and analytical methods to issues in financial theory and practice. Students specialize in research in areas such as corporate finance, asset pricing, investments, financial institutions, and derivatives. In addition to rigorous coursework, students are expected to make significant progress on their dissertations throughout the program. Students also gain valuable teaching experience in undergraduate finance courses during their time in the program.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Finance

description: The Ph.D. in Marketing program is designed to prepare students for academic careers as professors of marketing at leading research universities. Our program emphasizes rigorous training in theoretical foundations, quantitative methods, and advanced research techniques essential for conducting impactful research in contemporary marketing issues. Students work closely with faculty mentors, engaging in various research projects that often lead to publications in top-tier journals. The curriculum covers a broad range of topics, including consumer behavior, marketing strategy, international marketing, and research methodology, ensuring graduates are well-versed in diverse areas of marketing scholarship. Graduates from our program have successfully secured positions at reputable academic institutions globally, reflecting the quality and rigor of our training.
Accreditation status: The College of Business Administration at Kent State University is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB Accreditation is the hallmark of excellence in business education, and has been earned by less than five percent of the world's business programs.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Marketing

description: The Master of Arts in Economics degree at Kent State University provides students with a strong theoretical and empirical foundation for a career as a professional economist in government or private industry or for further graduate study at the doctoral level. The program emphasizes both advanced economic theory and quantitative applications. The M.A. program requires 30 credit hours of coursework. Students choose between a thesis option or a non-thesis option. The non-thesis option requires students to pass comprehensive examinations in microeconomic theory, macroeconomic theory and econometrics.
Program name: Master of Arts in Economics

description: The Master of Science in Business Analytics degree program is designed to meet the growing need for professionals with strong analytical skills in the evolving field of business analytics.
